_comment: The Fix-issues prompt model: depth levels + the scope/action text blocks the wizard assembles into the agent prompt. Single source for both front-ends; the assembly order/conditions live as a tiny glue layer in each (see Issues.swift / issues.py). The scope axis is wider than the Review/Conflicts one because an issue's author association is a filter in its own right — 'all', 'mine', one user, everyone OUTSIDE the org, everyone INSIDE it, or one specific issue. Two filters narrow whichever scope is chosen (unassignedOnly, and bugs-only unless includeFeatures escalates it), and four action blocks decide what the run is allowed to do about what it finds.

depths.title: Quick pass
depths.blurb: Fix only what the code makes unambiguous. Nothing is run.
depths.fragment: Do a QUICK PASS on each issue: read the report, find the code it actually names, and fix only the ones whose cause is unambiguous from reading that code — a wrong constant, an inverted condition, a missing guard whose absence is visible on the page. You don't need to run or reproduce anything at this depth. The flip side is that you must be honest about the limit: an issue whose cause you cannot pin down by reading is one you LEAVE ALONE and report as needing a deeper pass, never one you guess at.

depths.title: Reproduce & fix
depths.blurb: A concrete repro per issue, before the fix and again after it.
depths.fragment: For each issue: build a CONCRETE REPRODUCTION from the report before you change anything — precise inputs / steps → the wrong behaviour, run for real — so you have proof the bug exists and proof of what it does. Then develop the fix, and re-run that SAME reproduction to confirm it lands. An issue you cannot reproduce is not fixed: say so and move on, rather than shipping a change against a guess.

depths.title: Deep · swarm per issue
depths.blurb: Repro before & after; swarm the review moves over your own fix.
depths.fragment: For each issue: build a CONCRETE REPRODUCTION from the report before you touch anything, develop the fix, and re-run that SAME reproduction to confirm it lands. Then put your own fix through the review moves in my CLAUDE.md with a swarm of agents (3–8) — claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability both ways, and what outlives the call — plus the absence pass (a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry, and the mutation). Treat what the swarm returns as leads, not verdicts: confirm each against the code, fix what is real, and keep dispatching fresh swarms at that issue until one full pass comes back clean.

depths.title: Full E2E · max
depths.blurb: Drive the bug in the real app; swarm until one clean pass.
depths.fragment: Maximum rigor. For each issue, "reproduced" has a strict meaning: DRIVE THE BUG THROUGH THE REAL ENTRY POINT and watch the failure happen first-hand — run the actual app (booting a simulator / emulator where the bug needs one) and trigger the fault for real. A code-reading argument, a mock, a stub or an isolated unit test does NOT clear this bar. Fix it, then re-run that same end-to-end reproduction to prove the fix lands. Put your own fix through the review moves in my CLAUDE.md with swarms of agents — claims vs code, nearest twin, non-happy paths, inputs, reachability both ways, and what outlives the call — plus the absence pass (a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry, and the mutation). Keep dispatching swarms until ONE pass comes back clean — that single clean pass ends the loop, so do not run a confirmation pass on top of it.

scope.single: Take issue #{issue} in {owner}/{repo}. Use the `gh` CLI to fetch it (`gh issue view {issue} --repo {owner}/{repo} --comments`), including every comment on it — a follow-up comment routinely carries the reproduction, the version, or the correction the opening post lacks.
scope.multi: In {owner}/{repo}, go through {scope}, and handle EACH one.
scope.scopeContributors: every currently-open issue opened from OUTSIDE the organisation — one whose author association on the issue is anything other than {orgList} (so CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIMER, NONE and the like all count as outside)
scope.scopeMembers: every currently-open issue opened from INSIDE the organisation — one whose author association on the issue is {orgList}

_enumerateComment: Which enumeration block goes in depends on whether the chosen scope needs an author association, because that one field is the reason a plain `gh issue list` is not enough: `gh issue list --json` has no authorAssociation field at all (verified against gh's own field list), so the association scopes have to come off the REST issues endpoint — which in turn returns pull requests alongside issues and needs them filtered out. A scope that does not need the association takes the simpler `gh issue list` path.

enumerate.plain: Enumerate them with `gh issue list --repo {owner}/{repo} --state open --limit 200{searchFlag} --json number,title,author,assignees,labels,createdAt`.
enumerate.association: Enumerate them from the REST issues endpoint, which is the only `gh` read that carries the author association: `gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=100" --paginate`. TWO things about that endpoint you must handle or the run goes wrong: it returns PULL REQUESTS alongside issues — every node carrying a `pull_request` key is a PR and must be skipped outright — and the field you are filtering on is spelled `author_association` there (the GraphQL spelling `authorAssociation` does not exist in the REST payload, and `gh issue list --json` has no such field at all, so neither of those is an option). Read `author_association` off each remaining node and keep only the ones matching the scope above.

blocks.unassigned: NARROW THAT SET TO THE UNASSIGNED ONES: an issue that already has an assignee is somebody else's to work, so SKIP IT — do not fix it, do not comment on it, do not touch it. Only issues whose assignee list is empty are in scope for this run. This is a hard filter, applied before anything else: an issue assigned to me counts as assigned and is skipped too, because something is already handling it.
blocks.assignSelf: CLAIM EACH ISSUE BEFORE YOU START ON IT: the moment you pick one up, assign it to me — `gh issue edit <n> --repo {owner}/{repo} --add-assignee @me` — and only then begin the work. This is what stops a second agent (or a person) starting the same issue while you are on it, so it happens FIRST, before the reproduction, not once you have a fix. If you end up abandoning an issue — you could not reproduce it, it turned out to be out of scope, you ran out of road — remove yourself again (`--remove-assignee @me`) so it goes back into the unassigned pool instead of sitting claimed by nobody working it.
blocks.bugsOnly: ONLY REAL BUG REPORTS ARE IN SCOPE. For every issue in front of you, decide what it actually is: a bug report describes something that behaves wrongly. SKIP every feature request, enhancement proposal, design discussion, question, support request and wishlist item entirely — they are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and must not be worked, however easy one looks. When an issue is ambiguous, treat it as out of scope and say so in the summary rather than implementing something nobody asked you to.
blocks.includeFeatures: FEATURE REQUESTS ARE IN SCOPE TOO on this run, not only bug reports — but they are held to a different standard than a bug, because a bug has a right answer and a feature does not. Take on an enhancement ONLY when the issue states clearly enough what is wanted that you can build the thing the reporter actually asked for, and when it fits how this codebase already works: extend or compose what is there rather than introducing a parallel abstraction beside it. Anything vague, speculative, or amounting to a redesign gets left alone and named in the summary as needing a decision from me — that call is mine, not yours. Questions, support requests and pure discussion are still out of scope.
blocks.bar: Hold to the bar in my CLAUDE.md throughout. DONE MEANS OBSERVABLE PROOF, never "should work": a fix counts only once the same reproduction that showed the bug is re-run and comes back clean, and you say which verification you ran. Fix the CLASS, not the instance — search the repo for every other call site, sibling backend or adjacent path of the same shape and fix them together, or name each one you are leaving and why. Bring every piece of prose the change touches into agreement with the new behaviour, and write it as a description of the code as it now stands, never as a narration of what changed. Delete anything the fix made unreachable. And run the project's own checks — format, lint, typecheck, tests, build — before you call an issue done.
blocks.cannotReproduce: AN ISSUE YOU CANNOT REPRODUCE IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE RUN — it is a result, and it has to be reported as one. Never paper over it with a speculative change: no fix goes in on a bug you were unable to make happen. Say exactly what you tried (the steps, the version, the environment) and what you observed instead, so the gap is something I can act on.
blocks.openPRs: Deliver each fix as its own focused pull request, opened as a DRAFT (`gh pr create --draft`) — ALWAYS draft, never a ready-for-review PR, and never mark one ready yourself. Each PR closes the issue it fixes: put a closing reference (`Fixes #<n>`) in its description, and give it a title and description that name the defect and quote the evidence — the reproduction that proved the bug, and the same reproduction re-run clean after the fix. SHIP A REGRESSION TEST WITH EVERY FIX, one that pins the exact behaviour the fix corrected: you established the wrong value when you reproduced the bug and the right one when you confirmed the fix, so assert the right one in a way the wrong one would VIOLATE (an exact value, count, order, type or status code — never an incidental property like `>= 1` or `contains something`, which the unfixed code already satisfied). Do not undo or weaken the fix to check that; argue it from the reproduction you already captured. RIGHT BEFORE you open each PR, verify it is NOT a DUPLICATE of an existing open PR: enumerate the repo's open PRs and compare their ACTUAL CODE, not their titles or descriptions (those routinely mislead) — read each plausible candidate's real diff with `gh pr diff <n>`. If one already lands the same fix, do NOT open a duplicate: skip it and tell me which PR already covers it. You MAY bundle fixes for closely-related issues into one PR when they share a root cause or area — that is better than splitting hairs — but never one mega-PR of unrelated fixes, and never a PR for a fix whose reproduction you could not run clean.
blocks.noPRs: This run opens NO pull requests and pushes NOTHING: do not commit, do not push, do not open a PR. Keep each fix in the working tree and hand it to me in the summary — which files it touches, what it changes, and the reproduction you ran before and after it. Nothing reaches the remote.
blocks.comment: Report the outcome ON THE ISSUE ITSELF, one comment per issue you actually worked (`gh issue comment <n> --repo {owner}/{repo}`), so the reporter learns what happened without waiting for me. Say what you reproduced, what the cause turned out to be, and where the fix is — the PR number when there is one. If you could not reproduce it, say what you tried and what you saw instead, and ask for the one specific detail that would let you get further. Never post a bare "fixed" or "cannot reproduce" with nothing behind it, and never comment on an issue you did not work.
blocks.noAttribution: No AI attribution anywhere in git/GitHub — commits and PRs authored as me, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with" taglines.
blocks.diplomatTag: Diplomat attribution tag — a REQUIRED exception to the no-attribution rule, for GitHub commentary only. Do NOT tag PR titles — leave every pull-request title exactly as you would write it. End every pull-request DESCRIPTION with a footer: after the body, a blank line, a horizontal rule on its own line (`---`), a blank line, then this exact last line — `<sub>Made by Diplomat. Like what you're seeing? [Give it a try](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat).</sub>`. In that footer the word Diplomat is PLAIN TEXT (not a link); ONLY "Give it a try" is a Markdown link, pointing to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat. For every standalone comment you post instead (an issue comment, or a review / reply comment), BEGIN it with the exact prefix `\[[Diplomat](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat){model}\]: `, copied character for character — the `\[` and `\]` are literal brackets, only the word Diplomat is a Markdown link (to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat), anything after that link is plain text, and a colon and a space close it — followed by the text you would otherwise have written, so it renders as "[Diplomat{model}]: <your text>". This is the ONE sanctioned attribution; it applies to posted PR-description / comment text ONLY and never changes PR titles, commit messages, commit authorship, or the no-Co-Authored-By / no-"Generated with" git rules, which remain in force.
blocks.summary: At the very end, give me one consolidated report covering EVERY issue the scope above put in front of you, with each one in exactly one bucket: fixed (with the reproduction you ran and where the fix landed), reproduced but not fixed (and what stopped you), could not reproduce (what you tried, what you saw), and skipped (which filter took it out — assigned to someone, not a bug, out of scope). An issue that fell out of the scope silently is a gap in this report, not an issue that did not exist.
